To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The photoreactivating enzyme is a protein, 2) the photoreactivating system is localized in the cytoplasm, and 3) photoreactivation is not an essential process in the life cycle of E. coli B/r.

(i) photoreactivation (ii) in bacteria (iii) of pyrimidine heteroadducts (iv) is a light‐dependent reaction (v) that is mediated by photolyase (vi) and is catalyzed by the enzyme photoreactivating enzyme (vii) in a wavelength dependent manner.
photoreactivation (pr) is an enzyme that repairs DNA damage in the presence of light.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of a new class of photoreactivating enzyme inhibitors, the pyrimidine heteroadducts.
the development of novel synthetic routes to heterocyclic compounds.
the study of the mechanism of photoreactivation of u.v. induced damage in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photoreactivating light is not a specific photoreactivator, but that the photoreactivation effect is due to the photoenzymatic removal of pyrimidine heteroadducts, and that the photoreactive enzyme is a photolyase.
the action of photoreactivating light in bacteria is due solely to the photoreactivation of pyrimidine heteroadducts.
photoreactivation of u.v.‐induced pyrimidine dimmers in DNA of bacteria and phages is a photoenzymatic process, catalyzed by a protein, which is not a photolyase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PR of u.v. killing in bacteria is not a single‐molecule event.
PR of u.v. killing in E. coli B/r is due to the photoenzymatic repair of pyrimidine heteroadducts.

the u.v. killing of E. coli B/r by a 313 nm light dose of 0.5–1.0 J/m2 is not due to the action of a photoreactivating light, but to an action which is independent of the wavelength and dose of light.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to show that the PR gene in E. coli is a photoreactivation gene.
photoreactivating light is not a cure-all for the effects of UV radiation, but it can be used as a tool to study the effects of UV light on DNA.

the action spectrum of photoreactivation of the heteroadduct is very similar to that of pyrimidine dimer photoreactivation, suggesting that the same photoreactivating enzyme repairs both photoproducts.
